sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The dense CR2 frontier and sparse CR2-ratio theorem give unconditional variance-estimation comparisons for the homogeneous fixed-size design; no Gaussian counterpart is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact PAME variance proof uses complete-randomization algebra, but this note claims no Gaussian analogue.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper proves asymptotic normality for conventional two-stage finite-population sampling with fixed stage-specific values.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: No Gaussian analogue is claimed because randomly assembled disjoint groups generate composition-indexed scores rather than fixed stage-specific values.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The dense CR2 frontier shows the nonextension to positive-density finite-pool competition; it does not refute the working-model guarantee.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The dense CR2 frontier treats randomly formed disjoint groups and identifies the additional projection correction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The one-realization lower bound supplies a new positive-density nonextension certificate for exact variance estimation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The one-realization lower bound instead uses equal observation mixtures and separated dense PAME variance limits.

body.tldr: When a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned, randomly formed groups do not behave as independent regression clusters. The normalized Kneser operator gives an exact design variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order. Unconditionally, scalar equal-group CR2 converges to the independent-group variance: it is conservative at positive density and ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible; at zero density it is ratio-consistent under \(N_n/n\to0\), without \(N_n^2/n\to0\). No Gaussian, studentization, or Wald-coverage result is claimed. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) call returns this scalar CR2 formula exactly, and the eight-unit witness has true variance \(1/7\) but expected CR2 \(2/7\). An equal-observation Rademacher construction yields a new positive-density nonextension lower bound: no one-realization estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent for exact variance over the full dense class, already on an additive no-interference subclass.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} obtains PAME inference by coupling the disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation omits the first-order finite-pool covariance present when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), and an independent-cluster CR2 calculation does not restore it. Existing independent-cluster and conventional two-stage sampling central-limit theorems do not provide an unconditional Gaussian result for arbitrary bounded composition-indexed schedules.
project_justification.niche: Disjointness is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice. This makes the exact causal variance and the CR2 discrepancy computable degree by degree under the assignment law, without introducing a superpopulation or a Gaussian approximation. The same geometry isolates the unobserved degree-one cross-arm energy that obstructs uniform exact-variance recovery from one partition.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted PAME variance, a schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense projection expansion, the unconditional scalar CR2 probability limit and its sharp ratio-consistency frontier, and the zero-density CR2 ratio result without a birthday-scale condition. It verifies the precise versioned software consumer and the \(n=8\) witness. Finally, equal observed-data mixtures with separated positive-density variance limits and a nondegenerate first-sign certificate prove an all-statistic nonextension lower bound. The paper deliberately makes no Gaussian, studentization, or Wald-coverage claim.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 allows a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, its Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive results concern the homogeneous fixed-size subcase and are unconditional variance statements: exact Kneser covariance, the dense projection expansion, the CR2 ratio frontier, and zero-density CR2 ratio consistency under only \(N_n/n\to0\). They do not import or claim a Gaussian extension. \cite{Ohlsson1989} proves a conventional two-stage finite-population sampling central limit theorem with fixed stage-specific values; it does not cover composition-indexed scores generated by randomly assembling disjoint groups, and no Gaussian theorem is imported from it here. The slice-harmonic architecture comes from \cite{Filmus2016}, while Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum; the causal covariance quadratic form and dense projection limit are derived here. Complete-randomization algebra is informed by \cite{LiDing2017}, without invoking its finite-population central limit theorem. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the exact software assembly, adjustment, bread, and scaling semantics. \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} calibrates CR2 under an independent-cluster working covariance model, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives a fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison; neither model includes positive-density competition among disjoint random groups. Accordingly, the lower bound here is a new positive-density nonextension result, not a contradiction of the \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} guarantee on its stated domain or of the birthday-sparse \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} theorem. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither gives the equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound here. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, while global completion of a composition-indexed group table is distinct. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: its exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and the higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges only at the \(G_n\)-scale, where the negative degree-one eigenvalue is the sole surviving correction. The results establish variance expansions and variance-estimator ratios, not a central limit theorem, studentized limit, or Wald coverage. The Rademacher variance limits separate only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The impossibility certificate is proved on additive no-interference schedules and transfers upward to the arbitrary bounded composition class, but it does not identify an optimal conservative variance bound. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation statement is an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is only a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results remain restricted to homogeneous fixed group size.
body.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample PAME variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance and ratio expansions are design-based conclusions for fixed composition-indexed potential outcomes under the stated homogeneous random-partition design. At \(\rho=0\), CR2 is ratio-consistent under \(N_n/n\to0\) without requiring \(N_n^2/n\to0\); this is a variance-estimation result only. No centered Gaussian limit, CR2 studentization law, or Wald-coverage claim remains. The software identity is confined to the stated unweighted equal-group intercept-plus-binary-treatment fit and the versioned package semantics. The one-realization impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). It is a positive-density nonextension lower bound proved on additive no-interference schedules, with a high-probability design region where the first observed sign has both support probabilities bounded below and conditional variance bounded away from zero; it therefore transfers to the full arbitrary bounded composition class. It does not contradict \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} in its birthday-sparse regime or \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} under its independent-cluster working model. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.
